title: What remains after Nepal’s Gen Z protests? Survivors reflect one year later

headline: Nepal Reflects on Gen Z Protests Anniversary

pages.text: In September 2025, many young people in Nepal started protests. They were unhappy about government corruption. The protests began because of a ban on social media. Soon, students and Gen Z members joined in. Sadly, the protests became violent. Police and protesters fought, and many people were hurt.

imageProvenance.credit: Nepal's Gen Z protests against corruption in Bharatpur, south-central Nepal. Image via Wikipedia by Himal Subedi.

pages.text: Liza Adhikari was 21 years old when she was shot during the protests. She was near the Parliament building. The bullet hurt her arm very badly. She had to go to India for surgery on her nerves. She still cannot go back to her university classes. She feels sad about what happened, but she is trying to be strong.

Shantanu, an 18-year-old student, was also hurt. He was in Itahari when he was shot in the jaw. He had to have surgery to help him breathe and eat. It is hard for him to work on his family farm now. Another person, a police officer named Riya, was also hurt by stones during the fighting.

On September 8, 2026, Nepal held a special day to remember these events. Many people died or were injured in 2025. Today, the country is still talking about who is responsible for the violence. For the survivors, life is different now, but they are moving forward.

evidence: In September 2025, Nepal was gripped by nationwide protests led largely by students and members of Gen Z .
Among those caught in the violence was Liza Adhikari, 21, who was shot by an SLR bullet while standing opposite the Parliament Secretariat building.
With limited options available, she eventually traveled to India, where she recently underwent brachial plexus surgery .
A1-A2.headline: Nepal Remembers Young People’s Protests

pages.text: On September 8, 2026, Nepal observed its first Gen-Z Martyrs’ Day. This public holiday marked one year since nationwide protests transformed the country’s social and political landscape. What began in September 2025 as a reaction to a social media ban quickly evolved into a massive movement against government corruption and inefficiency. Led by students and Gen Z, the demonstrations eventually turned into violent confrontations with police, resulting in severe human rights violations.
pages.caption: Nepal's Gen Z protests against corruption in Bharatpur, south central Nepal. Image via Wikipedia by Himal Subedi. CC BY SA 4.0.

imageProvenance.credit: Nepal's Gen Z protests against corruption in Bharatpur, south-central Nepal. Image via Wikipedia by Himal Subedi.

pages.text: The human cost of these protests remains visible today. Liza Adhikari, a 21-year-old student, was shot near the Parliament Secretariat. The injury caused permanent damage to her arm, requiring complex surgery in India to repair her brachial plexus. She has been unable to return to her studies at Kathmandu University, carrying both physical and emotional scars.

Similarly, 18-year-old Shantanu from Itahari suffered a severe jaw injury after being shot during a protest. His recovery involved multiple surgeries and a long period of rehabilitation, which continues to affect his daily life and work on his family farm. The violence also impacted those on the other side. Riya, a police constable, was injured by stones while on duty in Kathmandu.

While the government has provided some medical support, the path to justice remains unclear. An inquiry commission recommended legal action against high-ranking officials, but a later review panel found insufficient evidence for criminal charges. As the nation reflects on the 19 lives lost on that day, survivors like Liza and Shantanu continue to navigate their uncertain futures.

evidence: The movement began with the government’s ban on social media platforms , but it quickly grew, without a leader , into a broader expression of public frustration over government corruption and inefficiency.
The protests then descended into confrontations with police officers that escalated and resulted in unlawful use of force, including severe human rights violations .
The bullet struck her from behind, tore through her body, and exited through the front, leaving behind an injury that cannot simply be stitched away.
B1-B2.headline: Nepal Reflects on Gen Z Protests Anniversary

pages.text: Nepal commemorated its inaugural Gen-Z Martyrs’ Day on September 8, 2026, a solemn anniversary marking the systemic upheaval triggered by the nationwide protests of September 2025. Initially sparked by a government-imposed ban on social media, the movement rapidly transcended its origins, coalescing into a leaderless outcry against pervasive government corruption and the perceived impunity of political elites.

imageProvenance.credit: Nepal's Gen Z protests against corruption in Bharatpur, south-central Nepal. Image via Wikipedia by Himal Subedi.

pages.text: The subsequent escalation into violent clashes between protesters and law enforcement resulted in documented human rights violations and a significant loss of life, with 19 fatalities recorded on September 8 alone. The personal narratives of survivors underscore the enduring consequences of the state’s response. Liza Adhikari, a 21-year-old undergraduate, sustained a life-altering injury from an SLR bullet near the Parliament Secretariat.

The trauma necessitated specialized brachial plexus surgery in India, as the nerve damage threatened her long-term physical mobility. Her academic trajectory remains suspended, overshadowed by the psychological and physical burdens of her recovery. Parallel to her experience is that of Shantanu, an 18-year-old from Itahari, whose life was irrevocably altered by a gunshot wound to the jaw.

His arduous recovery, involving tracheostomy and tissue grafting, serves as a poignant reminder of the violence that permeated regions beyond the capital. The quest for accountability remains a contentious issue in the post-protest political climate. While a judicial inquiry commission recommended the prosecution of high-level officials, including former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli, subsequent legal reviews have stalled, citing insufficient evidence for criminal liability.

This lack of resolution leaves survivors in a state of limbo, balancing their personal healing with the broader, unresolved demands for justice. As these individuals navigate their respective paths—Liza grappling with regret, and Shantanu pursuing engineering despite his scars—the anniversary serves as a stark reflection on the fragility of Nepal’s political stability and the lingering trauma of its youth.

evidence: The brachial plexus is a network of nerves that carries signals from the spinal cord to the shoulder, arm and hand, allowing movement and sensation.

In an online interview with the author from a hospital in India, Adhikari told Global Voices that the bullet had severely damaged the bones in her upper arm and doctors had told her that the veins were no longer functioning properly.
Her chances of making a full recovery, she was told, remain uncertain.
